paper.authors_full: Mia Magdalena Bangerl, Leonie Disch, Tamara David, Viktoria Pammer-Schindler
paper.title: CreAItive Collaboration? Users' Misjudgment of AI-Creativity Affects Their Collaborative Performance
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2025), ACM
paper.version_read: Published ACM proceedings version, CHI '25, April 26–May 01, 2025, Yokohama, Japan; DOI 10.1145/3706598.3713886; 17 pages (PDF p. 1). Received 12 September 2024; revised 10 December 2024; accepted 16 January 2025 (PDF p. 17).
paper.one_line_finding: The paper reports no significant main-test differences in AUT fluency (14.6 vs 12.7), originality (3.7 vs 3.7), or flexibility (10.0 vs 9.4), but lower AI-group elaboration immediately (2.1 vs 3.8; U = 924.0, p = 0.005) and after AI removal (2.8 vs 4.7; U = 970.0, p = 0.012), with no significant retention difference three weeks later (1.9 vs 2.2), although the elaboration tests have unresolved analysis units (pp. 8-10, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.3 and Figures 4, 8, 12).
paper.shared_samples: S1 shares no participants with another paper as far as the document states. S2 summarizes the pre-study published separately as Bangerl, Stefan, and Pammer-Schindler (2024), 'Explorations in human vs. Generative AI creative performances: A study on human-AI creative potential', CHI TREW 2024 workshop paper (reference [7]).

studies.label: Main experiment: collaborative alternate uses with ChatGPT-4, followed by unaided immediate and three-week retention post-tests

counts_source.quote: The valid sample consisted of 52 dyads/104 participants, with 26 dyads/52 participants per experimental condition.

arms.name: Experimental AI group
arms.description: Self-formed dyads randomly assigned to off-the-shelf ChatGPT-4 in a chat window during the main AUT; free prompting, no researcher pre-prompting, and no copy-pasting into the answer box. AI was removed for both post-tests (PDF pp. 4-6, Sections 3 and 4.2).

arms.name: Control non-AI group
arms.description: Dyads randomly assigned to the same AUT and interface without AI; both post-tests were also unaided (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 4.2.2-4.2.4).

studies.task: Computer Science students produced alternate uses for fork, flower pot, and suitcase as dyads, then for a glass bottle in an immediate unaided dyad post-test, and for key, brick, and gymnastics ball individually in an unaided online retention test three weeks later (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 4.2).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF p. 5, Section 4.2.2. Model release year is not stated. Reference [80] on PDF p. 16 gives a March 2024 version of gpt-4 but is cited for ChatGPT in general on PDF p. 1; the Methods do not confirm that version.

preregistration.where: AsPredicted, https://aspredicted.org/msym-tbc2.pdf (PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF p. 13, Section 6.4). The paper explicitly states that hypotheses were preregistered. Direct retrieval and the archive.org mirror named in forms/data/c032.json both failed with network socket permission errors during reconciliation.

The second verifier correctly flags that null is outside the allowed se_basis vocabulary. not_reported is also unsupported because uncertainty is printed, and no other allowed code can be confirmed. se_basis remains null solely as an unresolved placeholder outside the schema, not as an accepted code or a rejected verifier flag. The extraction rules leave this case open: they provide no code for reported uncertainty with an unconfirmed inferential basis. Resolution requires an explicit rule for representing that case or additional source evidence establishing the test unit and handling of dyad dependence. Primary status is not stated. The paper identifies preregistered flexibility and originality hypotheses, but does not designate primary or secondary outcomes; the registration itself could not be retrieved.

not_extracted.what: S2 pre-study: AI-only chatbots versus human dyads, including AUT elaboration (S2-O1) and originality (S2-O2)
not_extracted.reason: No people were randomized to AI assistance: the chatbots worked alone and their answers were compared with human dyads. This is ai_vs_human context, outside Phase 2 extraction (PDF p. 4, Section 4.1). The pre-study was published separately as reference [7] (PDF p. 15).

not_extracted.what: S1 main-test fluency: top-quartile AI versus control comparison
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup comparison of high performers, not the full randomized sample. Its means and SD statement cannot replace full-sample values (PDF p. 8, Section 5.1.1).

not_extracted.what: S1 main-test flexibility: top-quartile AI versus control comparison
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup comparison of high performers, not the full randomized sample. Its means and SD statement cannot replace full-sample values (PDF p. 8, Section 5.1.1).

not_extracted.what: S1 perception-of-AI questionnaires, perceived AI roles and helpfulness, self-assessed ability to generate the AI answers, intended future AI use, and interim AI-use questionnaire
not_extracted.reason: Self-reports, attitudes, intentions, or AI-use reports rather than creativity scored on produced task output. The interim questionnaire is described without reported results (PDF p. 6, Sections 4.2.4 and 4.4.2; PDF p. 10, Section 5.2 and Figure 13).

not_extracted.what: S1 prompt specificity scores and prompt-type counts
not_extracted.reason: Process measures of how the AI group prompted ChatGPT, not creativity scores on AUT output and not a randomized between-arm comparison (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.5.4 and Table 1; PDF pp. 11-12, Section 5.3 and Tables 3-4).

not_extracted.what: S1 human-AI interaction patterns, timing of AI use, generation time, and reported collaboration strategies
not_extracted.reason: Process and self-report analyses, without a randomized contrast on the creativity of task output (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.5.4 and Table 2; PDF pp. 10-11, Section 5.3).

not_extracted.what: S1 handling of AI-generated answers and human/AI contributions to entered AUT answers
not_extracted.reason: Table 5 reports AI-arm-only process counts and proportions, with no corresponding control contrast. Its entered-answer total is not substituted for the scored main-test fluency mean in Figure 4 (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 5.3 and Table 5).

not_extracted.what: S1 AI-answer acceptance-rate association with main-test fluency
not_extracted.reason: Spearman correlation within the AI arm, not a randomized AI-versus-comparison effect. Its uncertainty also has an unresolved inconsistency with the dyad label (PDF p. 11, Section 5.3 and Figure 14).

not_extracted.what: S1 prompt-specificity associations with AUT dimensions
not_extracted.reason: Within-AI-arm process correlations, not randomized configuration contrasts; the text reports no correlations without numerical test results (PDF p. 11, Section 5.3).

not_extracted.what: S1 demographic and prior private AI-use group differences and associated correlation/moderation checks
not_extracted.reason: Baseline characteristics and confounding/moderation checks are not eligible full-sample contrasts on scored creative output (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

open_items: The initial randomized and excluded people/dyad counts are not printed. The analyzed valid sample and clusters_per_arm are supported by PDF p. 6, Section 4.3; the language-based inclusion rule is on PDF p. 5, Section 4.2.1.

The main and immediate elaboration U statistics are incompatible with an ordinary Mann-Whitney comparison at the stated dyad counts. Confirm the inferential rows, statistic convention, and treatment of dyad dependence, and obtain uncertainty at the randomized-dyad level (PDF pp. 7-9, Sections 4.5.1 and 5.1.1-5.1.2). No count is reconstructed from a test statistic or p-value. Second-round review confirms that s1_elaboration_main_ai_vs_control.se_basis and s1_elaboration_immediate_ai_vs_control.se_basis are unresolved schema exceptions: null is outside the allowed vocabulary, while not_reported is false because the tests and exact p-values are printed. No permitted replacement is established by the supplied source. Both nulls remain placeholders pending an explicit extraction-rule decision for reported uncertainty with an unconfirmed basis, or additional source evidence identifying the inferential observations and treatment of dyad dependence. The two reverify flags are valid and are not dismissed as false positives.

Immediate post-test fluency has narrative means and SDs, but the SD computational rows are not identified explicitly. The scored work was produced by dyads and the allowed sd_level vocabulary has no team category; sd_level remains null pending clarification (PDF pp. 7 and 9, Sections 4.5.1 and 5.1.2).

Retention analyzed counts and attrition are not confirmed. The procedure and Section 5.1.3 describe individuals, while Figure 12 labels dyads and Figure 1 depicts individuals. Confirm the number of analyzed people and aggregation before using this comparison (PDF pp. 5-6 and 9-10).

Except for immediate post-test fluency, arm means occur only in figures and are left null under extraction rule 1. Obtain text/table values and missing full-sample dispersion and uncertainty; subgroup statistics cannot replace these (PDF pp. 8-10, Section 5.1 and Figures 4-12).

Supplementary Materials are referenced but are not included in or embedded in the supplied PDF. No matching supplement was found under the paper identifiers in the local literature folder. The publisher landing-page request failed with a network socket permission error. Its scoring and statistical contents remain unverified (PDF pp. 5-7 and 10).

The paper preregisters flexibility/originality hypotheses but does not expressly designate primary outcomes. Requests to the linked AsPredicted registration and the archive.org mirror both failed with network socket permission errors. primary_outcome is null and all preregistered_primary fields are not_stated (PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF p. 13, Section 6.4).
The retention delay is printed as three weeks, not days; delay_days remains null because unit conversion is prohibited (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.4).

The exact experimental ChatGPT-4 version and release year are not established. Reference [80] gives a documentation/model version, while the Methods identify only off-the-shelf ChatGPT-4; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF pp. 1, 4-5 and 16).
AUT coder identities and reliability are not reported in the available main text. Only a detailed scoring description is explicitly referred to the supplement (PDF p. 7, Sections 4.5.1-4.5.2).
The retention task is described as unaided, but prevention/checking of AI use and results of the interim AI-use questionnaire are not reported (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 4.2 and 4.2.4).

review_corrections.basis: The printed U exceeds the range possible with the stated dyad counts, so the test's unit cannot be established (third verifier and fixer agree).
As above (U = 924.0 at 26 dyads per arm).

review_resolutions.resolution: Vocabulary gap, not a data error: both agree that the paper prints a test whose unit of analysis it does not establish. se_basis `unclear` now covers this case (2026-10-10); the record uses it and is never pooled.
